### `afkconvoy help worker-codex`

How the fleet starts Codex workers. Shared launch rules are in [`afkconvoy help worker-launch`](help:worker-launch).

#### A bound repo

A Codex worker — of a role whose range runs it Codex — is the session you would have at a terminal, not `codex exec`: the fleet sends to a worker after it starts. It starts in its role's directory like any other:

```
cd <the role's copy> && export CODEX_HOME=<the fleet's own>
  <the stage's facts> && <worker launch command> --add-dir <the worktree>
  --dangerously-bypass-hook-trust
  --config 'projects={"<the role's copy>"={trust_level="trusted"}}'
  --config 'project_doc_fallback_filenames=["CLAUDE.md"]'
  --config 'project_root_markers=[]'
  [--config 'developer_instructions="<the repo's own rules, the team rules>"']
  --config 'hooks={PreToolUse=[<what asks afkconvoy guard, and orca's status
    report>], <each other event a session's state changes at>=[<the report>]}'
  --config features.memories=false
  --config skills.bundled.enabled=false
  [--config 'skills.config=[<each skill of yours the role's stands for, off>]']
  --model <the fleet's selected model>
  [--config 'model_reasoning_effort="<your current effort>"']
```

`projects` and `--dangerously-bypass-hook-trust` answer on the line what Codex would ask at its terminal — whether it trusts the folder, and a review of its hooks — and have it load the role's own limits (`.codex/hooks.json`). The next two have it load its role's rules — the CLAUDE.md of the directory it starts in — and those of no directory above. Codex loads rules from no directory added to it, so `developer_instructions` says the other two to it, each as what it is and with its file: the repo's own rules — the worktree's AGENTS.md, or its CLAUDE.md where it holds none — and the team rules (the team's CLAUDE.md), as they stand when the worker starts. A repo and a team with none are told none.

The hook named asks `afkconvoy guard` before every tool call: one the guard refuses, or cannot be asked of, is not made. It is on the line and in no file, so no worker starts without it. The report is the hook orca installed to hear of a Codex session's state (~/.orca/agent-hooks/codex-hook.sh), which orca names in your own hooks and a worker loads none of: it is given ten seconds, and refuses no call, whatever it does; where orca installed none, nothing is told, and a worker's state is read off its terminal.

Every Codex session has a fresh user directory under its worktree's `.afkconvoy-tmp`, so a `/model` choice saved by Codex is private to that session. The directory of a bound worker holds links to your login (auth.json), your skills (skills) and your rules (AGENTS.override.md, AGENTS.md), and no hook or configuration of yours, so no provider you defined in config.toml. Under a team or role that says `host_user: false` it holds your login alone. The shared cache directories harness/codex-host-user and harness/codex still serve listing, research and recovery probes; workers never load their config.toml, including model or effort left there by older workers. A login Codex keeps in a keyring is in no file, and is no worker's: the start refuses, and `doctor` says so. A bound worker's memories are off.

#### Model and effort

The fleet selects the model by host kit order, role eligibility and casting, and passes it explicitly with `--model` for both bound and unbound repos. No config.toml selects a worker's model. While the host kit places no Codex model — none listed yet, or research pending — a Codex worker starts with no `--model`, on Codex's own default, and its model is recorded as null with the source `codex_default`. `afkconvoy kit` lists and researches its models now, and the next tick also lists an entry with no Codex models without waiting for the daily refresh, with an hour between unsuccessful tries. Discovery filters the server catalog to model names before it reaches terminal scrollback.

Reasoning effort has a different source: every launch reads `model_reasoning_effort` from your own `~/.codex/config.toml` and passes it with `--config`. Changing that file changes the next worker without restarting the fleet. With no setting, Codex uses its selected model's default. This applies even with `host_user: false`. The fleet keeps no effort setting of its own. An unbound worker's fresh user directory holds the same allowed login, skill and rule links, and no other user settings; its `/model` writes change neither your configuration nor another worker's. Existing workers keep the settings they started with.

The same model and effort rules hold for a patrol, a consult, a watch and the caster's headless Codex call. The caster uses a fresh login-only directory and reads the user's effort when it makes that call. Model listing and recovery probes remain host capability checks. The watch researches models with its web tools and places its checked research through `afkconvoy kit --research <file>`.

`plan` and `doctor` list started sessions under `codex_workers`: issue, worktree, model, effort, model_source (`fleet_selection`) and effort_source (your config file and key, or `codex_default`). Each row also names its harness and codex_home, the private session directory. A later edit of your own config does not relabel an existing worker. If `/model` saves a different choice, it is shown with that session's private config as the source. `plan` also gives a Codex frontier issue's next-launch settings under `codex`. The panel shows each Codex worker's model and effort with the same sources. A malformed Codex configuration file or a non-string effort refuses the start and names the file to fix.

#### An unbound repo 

A Codex worker of an unbound repo, starts in its worktree with the same allowed user links in a fresh directory, and the same trust and session setup. Nothing is written to your Codex configuration, even when Codex has never seen the worktree:

```
export CODEX_HOME=<this session's directory> && <worker launch command> --model <the fleet's selected model>
  --dangerously-bypass-hook-trust
  --config 'projects={"<the worktree>"={trust_level="trusted"}}'
  --config 'project_doc_fallback_filenames=["CLAUDE.md"]'
  --config features.memories=false --config skills.bundled.enabled=false
```

There is no role or team to add, no stage facts and no fleet guard hook: these workers start where their repo's own rules and skills load. Rule discovery keeps its normal roots, so the worktree's AGENTS.md, or its CLAUDE.md fallback, is read normally. The host user's skills and rules are linked as above. The fleet checks the command's flags before starting these Codex workers too.

#### Skill discovery

Codex finds skills in `.agents/skills/` and `.codex/skills/` of the directory it starts in, and not in `.claude/skills/`, where a role's are: the role's copy a Codex worker starts in is Codex's own (<commit>-role+codex-<path>), and holds a link, `.agents/skills` to `../.claude/skills`, made once with the copy. The role's repo holds nothing for it; a role that holds either directory itself is left as it is, and a worker is shown the skills there. `skills.bundled.enabled=false` leaves out the skills Codex carries. Codex shows both of two skills of one name, so a skill of yours named as one of the role's is turned off on the line, by the path of its file (`--config 'skills.config=[{path="<its SKILL.md>",enabled=false}]'`): the role's is the one a worker is shown. One thing of yours a Codex worker loads even under `host_user: false`: the skills of your home (~/.agents/skills). Codex finds them wherever its user directory is and has no way to be told to leave them out, and the fleet does not work around it — so on two hosts such a worker may be shown different skills besides its role's. Keep none there on a host whose Codex workers must be shown their role's alone.

The stock command runs Codex in no sandbox: a worker is limited by the guard, and a host that wants a sandbox says a command of its own. A command you give for Codex must take `--add-dir`, `--dangerously-bypass-hook-trust`, `--config` and `--model`.

### `afkconvoy help worker-proxy`

Which hosts a worker reaches past the proxy: a setting of one start on one host, said by `--worker-no-proxy`, which `run`, `tick`, `dispatch`, `restart` and `switch` take to start workers with, and `plan` and `doctor` to show what such a start would do. It is never a key of the repo's config: no proxy setting is read from the config or written to GitHub.

#### The flag

`--worker-no-proxy [HARNESS=]HOSTS` says a comma-separated list of hosts workers reach directly. The bare form is for the default harness; repeat it for other harnesses, never twice for one.

```
--worker-no-proxy dsh=api.deepseek.com,internal.example
```

#### What a worker is given

The worker's login shell extends its exported no_proxy and NO_PROXY with this list and exports the joined list under both names before it starts the worker. Every other proxy variable stays as it was. Without a list, both spellings stay untouched, except DSH's stock api.deepseek.com addition. Say `--worker-no-proxy dsh=` to turn that stock addition off. These settings apply to every worker, including patrols, consults and landing workers.

#### What `plan` and `doctor` show

Each answers `worker_no_proxy` — `doctor` under `host` — listing every harness: {harness, addition, no_proxy, NO_PROXY}. `addition` is the host list added, null when none is: a null addition leaves both inherited values alone. The other fields show the login shell's resulting comma-separated values. They describe a start now, with the flags given to that command and the host user's login shell exports.

### `afkconvoy help humans`

Every way the fleet stops for an answer, and the command a human or the host's watch uses.

#### Where to look

`afkconvoy doctor` lists every open issue that waits for a human under `waiting_on_human`, with `why` (what kind of wait, then the first sentence of the reason its comment gives), `url` (that comment, or an older failure report itself), since when and `answer`: the line to run for that issue. `afkconvoy plan` gives the same list; the panel shows it as "With a human". Waiting more than an hour is a finding.

An escalated issue carries the escalate label (`ready-for-human` unless renamed) in place of its flow label. Its comment says why; current comments end with the line to answer. `doctor` gives the current line, even where an older comment has none or names the issue before it moved to the tracker. Run every command below in a checkout of the repo, replacing what stands between < and >.

#### An escalation

A stage failed or declared `escalate`. A consult explicitly named by the stage is asked first about the work; an unbound repo, or a stage that names no consult, escalates immediately. There is no stock consult. The host's watch picks the issue up from `waiting_on_human` and answers it with the operator's authority. The comment says what failed or gives the question to answer.

A **fleet fault** escalates at once, with no consult asked and no consult claim taken: a worker start that failed again, a worktree trust gap. The comment and `doctor`'s `waiting_on_human` entry say it is a fleet fault and that the fix is on the host — trusting a worktree, switching a harness, waiting out a usage limit, or mending a build server. Fix it there, then hand the issue back with the line given. Another failed start escalates at once again; nothing new retries. A worker gone silent had its brief, so that hand-off still goes to its named consult first, as do an `escalate`, a tripped breaker, an impossible `blocked`, a refuted `already-satisfied`, a commit a stage may not leave and a changed workflow.

A watch is the operator for every repo on its host's checkout list (`afkconvoy run --help`, WATCH). It may fix the host cause of a fleet fault and hand the issue back with the current line `doctor` gives, checking the next tick dispatches or continues it. A lasting fix in any listed repo goes through its own checkout and landing turn; one that must reach an installed tool is followed through cutting, installation and a check on the new version. The watch may rule, hand an issue back, send it to a stage, close it or change its blocked-by, using the same commands as a human. Its ruling and sending start rework counts over as a human's do; it supplies no consult flag or role and team commits. Both the stock watch and a watch in the operator's directory leave only these four kinds to a human, list each with the question and answer line in their printed record, and act on none of them: spending money or needing an account, a credential or a person's hands; what cannot be undone; taking a secret or private data off the host; changing what a product is for or who it is for. `doctor` lists that record as what the watch did.

For a failure, fix what failed first: `afkconvoy rule` starts the same stage anew, and what failed it once fails it again. In an unbound repo there is no stage to run again: fix what the comment names and put the ready label back, with the line the comment ends with. A PR the escalation kept is not started anew: the next worker takes it up — it reads the issue's comments, merges the base branch, gates and lands in a turn — so say on the issue what is to be done on it.

#### An escalation with no position

An issue escalated before it entered any workflow of the team — the repo was unbound then, or it came from another repo — has no stage records: `afkconvoy show --issue <n>` says it has no position. `rule` and `send` refuse it and give the line that puts a flow label on it. Answer it with that line, as `doctor`'s `answer` gives it: with one workflow its flow label is filled in, ready to run; with several workflows, `why` lists each flow label to choose `<flow label>` from. `plan` and the panel give the same answer and choices. The issue starts at the chosen workflow's first stage.

Where its comment gives a line of its own, `doctor`'s is the current one: a comment written before the issue moved to the tracker names its old number and may name no tracker. Use the current issue number and tracker in the line `doctor` gives.

#### Answering an escalation

Every command a human or the watch runs to answer one, `<n>` the issue's number. Where the checkout's tracker is another repo (`afkconvoy run --tracker`), name it in every `gh` line — `--repo <owner>/<tracker>`, `repos/<owner>/<tracker>/…` — and give `gh issue create` the repo label too, `--label repo:<owner>/<repo>`: run in the checkout, `gh` acts on the checkout's own repo. The lines an escalation's comment, `plan` and `doctor` give name it already. A consult may run each, and any read-only command, the gate too; never commit, push or change the host.

- `afkconvoy rule --issue <n> --text-file <file>`: The stage runs again under your ruling; both rework counts start over (a consult's starts none over). `afkconvoy rule --help`.
- `afkconvoy send --issue <n> --stage <stage> --text-file <file>`: Put it at another stage, when the approach or workflow changed, or bring it back from a park. `afkconvoy send --help`.
- `gh issue close <n> --comment <why>`: Nothing is left to do on it: the fleet leaves a closed issue alone.
- `gh issue create --title <title> --body-file <file> --label <ready label>`: Open what it found outside this issue — a broken base branch, a host problem, a defect of afkconvoy — for the fleet to work.
- `gh issue edit <n> --body-file <file>`: Keep its body's "## Blocked by" in step with an edge added or removed.
- `gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues/<n>/dependencies/blocked_by -F issue_id=<id>`: Record it as blocked by the issue whose database id is `<id>`.
- `gh api -X DELETE repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues/<n>/dependencies/blocked_by/<id>`: Remove that edge: one whose waiting would never end, say.

#### Parked for evidence

A consult's close or park carries a reason and adds no rework. `plan` and `doctor` list parks under `waiting_on_human`. To bring one back in a bound repo, explicitly send it with new evidence or your reason (a plain comment does not bring it back):

```sh
afkconvoy send --issue <n> --stage <stage> --text-file <evidence-file>
```

#### A tripped breaker

Rework went past what the workflow allows — in total, or as rejections in a row by one stage — and the issue went to the consult in place of that rework, and escalates for the watch where the stage names no consult or it trips again after the consult ruled. The comment names the breaker and lists every rework with its stage and why. Answer as an escalation: `afkconvoy rule` with what settles it, or `afkconvoy send`. `afkconvoy doctor` says beforehand when an issue is one rework from a breaker.

#### A stage `by: human`

A workflow may give a stage to a human. An issue at one waits there, claimed by nobody, under its flow label and with no escalate label: only the lists above show it.

- `afkconvoy verdict pass --issue <n> --stage <stage> --text-file <file>`: Declare the stage's verdict: `pass`, or `reject` where the stage has that edge. The issue goes where the workflow leads from it. `afkconvoy verdict --help`.

#### A patrol's failed run

A run of a patrol that failed opens an issue of its own, under the escalate label, which says what failed. The patrol is not run again while that issue is open.

- `gh issue close <n>`: Once you have looked: the patrol runs again when it is next due. `afkconvoy plan` gives each patrol's standing.

#### A cut that failed

A cut that failed at a step, ran out of time or was ended from outside opens an issue of its own, under the escalate label, titled `afkconvoy: the cut of v<version> failed`: which step failed, why, what it did before, and the line that goes on from there. Its checkout is kept on the host that cut. No cut starts while that issue is open.

- `cd <its checkout> && afkconvoy cut --from <step>`: Once what failed it is fixed — the line the issue gives. It takes that step and the ones after it, and closes the issue once it took the last. `afkconvoy cut --help`.
- `gh issue close <n>`: Once you have looked and want the fleet to cut again from the start: the next tick that ends idle does, its kept checkout removed first. A PR of the failed cut still open is yours to close. A cut that failed at `publish` has pushed its tag: closed with no line run, that version stays unpublished, and the next cut is of the version after it, once more lands.

#### A fleet lock

An open issue under the lock label is a fleet lock: the fleet works lock issues only, and hands no other issue to a human, until the last one closes. A worker raises one when the fault is one every issue shares; a human may too:

```sh
afkconvoy lock --issue <n>
```

Closing a lock's issue ends it. A lock needs you when nothing can work its issue: it has no flow label or an open blocker. `afkconvoy doctor` gives a critical finding with a `fix` to run. Close a lock raised by mistake. `afkconvoy lock --help`.

#### A precedent to accept

Where the team names who proposes precedents, each ruling a human gives with `afkconvoy rule` is followed by a proposal: a PR on the team's repo that appends one entry to its precedents — the ruling in a sentence, when it applies, and a link to the ruling. Nothing waits on it: the stage that asked has already run again.

- `gh pr merge <pr> --repo <the team's repo>`: Merging accepts the precedent: every later stage reads it, and follows it in place of declaring `escalate` on the same question.
- `gh pr close <pr> --repo <the team's repo>`: The ruling was about that one issue, and no stage should follow it unasked.

The fleet never merges on the team's repo. `afkconvoy doctor` lists the team's open proposals under `proposals.open`: each PR, the issue and comment of its ruling, how long it has been open, and the merge and close commands. `afkconvoy doctor --all` lists them for every checkout on this host's checkout list. `afkconvoy panel` shows them under "With a human" too. Both read only and make no startup probe. Once the open proposals reach the team's `max_open`, doctor gives a finding and the panel says so: no further proposal starts until a human merges or closes one. `afkconvoy plan` lists the rulings being proposed or still to be proposed under `proposals`, with how each stands; it makes a startup probe where one is due.

#### An issue past the end of its workflow

A workflow that ended without a landing leaves its issue open: `gh issue close <n>`.

#### What not to do

For an issue with a position, do not move the labels by hand: its stage records say where it is, so one handed back with no ruling on record is escalated again. Rule on it, or send it. An escalation with no position needs a flow label first, as above.

### `afkconvoy help troubleshooting`

Start with `afkconvoy doctor`, in the checkout the fleet runs in: it reads everything and changes nothing. Each finding has a `fix` — a line to run, or a file and key to edit — and `evidence`. Below, a row for each: the words its `what` holds, why, and what to do. Then what a start refuses with, and what neither says.

#### What `doctor` finds — critical: the fleet does not work until it is fixed

- `is not installed`: A command the fleet needs is not on this host. Run `fix`: the line that installs it.
- `is not logged in`: `gh` or `claude` is logged out, as a login shell sees it. Run `fix`. Of `codex`: it has no login in ~/.codex/auth.json, the file a worker is given. One Codex keeps in a keyring is in no file: have Codex keep it in one, and run `fix`.
- `holds credentials for no provider`: A stage or a patrol runs on pi, logged in nowhere. Start `pi` and type `/login`.
- `is not running`: orca is not running, and every worker is started through it. Run `fix`.
- `cannot be asked about this checkout`: orca runs but did not say which repos it knows; `evidence` says why. Run `fix`.
- `does not know this checkout`: orca was never given the checkout worktrees are cut from. Run `fix`, once.
- `cannot start a worker`: The first word of a worker launch command resolves to nothing in a login shell, as an alias of your own shell's may. Name one that does: `afkconvoy run --help`.
- `cannot start a worker in its role`: In a bound repo the worker launch command must end in its harness, taking flags: the fleet adds what puts the worker in its role. `afkconvoy help worker-launch`.
- ``no `afkconvoy run` is alive``: The `run` of this host died holding claims. Start it here: it takes them back.
- `is broken`: This checkout's fleet instance panicked, its loop ended in an error, or its startup probe no longer passes; every other goes on, and the host runner starts it again after a backoff, when `evidence` says. Put right what `what` says, then run `fix`: a `run` starts it at once.
- `is public: its fleet instance works nothing`: GitHub says the repo this checkout's fleet reads and writes its issues in — its own, where it says no tracker — is public, so anyone can write what the fleet reads and its workers are told. Its fleet instance ends at its next check, within the hour, and every start of it is refused. Run `fix` with a private repo of yours, or make that repo private again: the next start of it works.
- `failed in each of the last`: One step fails tick after tick; `evidence` is its error, naming what refused. `fix`.
- `the team this repo names cannot be read`: The team's repo, or a role's, could not be read. `afkconvoy check` says which.
- `has a fault at its head`: A team's or a role's file is wrong on its default branch. `fix` is the file and key; `afkconvoy check` gives every fault. Push the edit: no stage starts until then.
- `stands and cannot be worked`: A fleet lock is on an issue no worker can be started on, so the fleet works nothing. `fix` gives the issue what it lacks; [`afkconvoy help humans`](help:humans).
- `the fleet's state cannot be read`: GitHub, the remote or the config failed to answer; `evidence` says which.
- `harness is down`: Identical refusals hold claims and pause it; a prompt probes every 5m. Run `fix`.

#### What `doctor` finds — warning: one issue or one patrol is held up

- `hot worker is past its limits`: A worker crossed a host resource limit. The watch receives its condition, duration, worktree, terminal and evidence and checks that work goes on.
- `admission has held back new workers`: One reason held admission for the host's span. The watch receives the host reading and evidence, once per episode.
- `the host has been under memory pressure`: Pressure lasted for the host's span independently of admission. The watch checks pressure itself, once per episode; it makes no worker hot.

A warning may be the fleet mid-step: run `doctor` again after a tick before you act on one.

- `ended at the exclusive bound`: A command held others up for the host's bound. Each occurrence in the last day has the command, runtime and number waiting in `evidence`. Run each step of a long measurement as its own `afkconvoy exclusive`. If a single gate or release build reaches it, check the host setting with `afkconvoy doctor` and change it with `afkconvoy run --exclusive-seconds N`, or `--exclusive-seconds default` to restore 1200s.

- `failed in tick`: A step failed, including a worker that could not start or take its brief. `evidence` is the error and `fix` is the line to try after correcting it: a failed dispatch can be run again, and a failed repair worker start uses `afkconvoy tick`. It stays visible across unrelated ticks until the step succeeds or the issue's work continues or ends. Three consecutive failed ticks make it critical instead.
- `has no worker`: A claim's worker is gone; a tick starts one. `fix` is for a claim it leaves so.
- `has been stopped for`: A worker stopped half an hour ago and its claim is still at work. Read its terminal; `fix` follows its verdict and progress. A `blocked` verdict whose blockers all closed names `dispatch`, which continues its worktree; open blockers name `park`. Only a worker eligible for a nudge names `nudge`; other cases name `tick`.
- `worker health is waiting for the operator`: A worker stopped past the observation bound, and neither the rules nor Jev — where the host settings name a Jev key command — classed it: there is no key command, it failed, TypeSafe failed, or Jev's answers settled nothing. `evidence` is that reason and the last line of its screen; `fix` names a key command where there is none, else the worker's screen to read. The watch starts on it. An hour on unchanged evidence escalates its issue.
- `the last tick started no worker`: Slots are free, the frontier is not empty, and nothing was dispatched: `evidence` is the tick's line, and `fix` the step that failed or the dispatch by hand.
- `follows no workflow of the team`: An issue's flow label names no workflow, or it has two. `afkconvoy flows` lists all.
- `longer than any stage before it took`: Nothing is wrong yet: an issue has been at one stage for long. `fix` shows it.
- `is one rework from a breaker`: The next `reject` escalates the issue. Nothing to do yet: [`afkconvoy help humans`](help:humans).
- `no harness can start this host's watch`: A look of the host runner called for a watch, and no harness of the host kit could start it or go on with it: each paused, with a fault on record, or failing to start, as `evidence` says. Nothing watches the host until one can: `afkconvoy kit` shows the host kit, and its `worker_health` the faults. The next look tries again (`afkconvoy run --help`, WATCH).
- `is paused on this host`: It refused every prompt: no worker starts on it till an hourly probe answers.
- `has unplaced models in the host kit`: The watch researches these listed models with its web tools and places or settles them through `afkconvoy kit --research <file>`. `afkconvoy kit --help` gives the checked JSON format and research states. Omitted models still await research; a harness with none placed runs its default model. Research runs during a watch started for other work, or starts one alone at most once a day. A malformed file writes nothing and names what to correct.
- `names no model the host kit holds`: A team's roster names a model by a name that matches no model the host kit holds for its harness, by its id or any other name; `evidence` gives the nearest names. The fleet never changes a roster: a tick opens one issue for it in the team's repo, which the team's own fleet works. `fix` is the file and key to correct.
- `has no harness on this host it holds limits for`: A role holds limits for no harness the host kit holds, so no worker of it starts and its stages wait; the rest go on. They go on by themselves once the host kit holds one: `afkconvoy kit`, or write the role's limits for one it holds.
- `matches nothing in the host kit`: A role's roster entry names only harnesses or models this host lacks, so the role runs the host kit whole, less what it holds no limits for. Add one with `afkconvoy kit`, or change the roster.
- `does not run: its last run failed`: The issue that reports a patrol's failed run is open. Look, then close it: `fix`.
- `cuts no version: its last cut failed`: The issue that reports the fleet's failed cut is open: it names the step that failed, why, and the line that goes on from there. Read it (`fix`), then run that line in the cut's checkout, which closes it once the cut is over; or close it, and the next idle tick cuts again from the start (`afkconvoy help humans`).
- `` have reached its `max_open` ``: A patrol is not run while that many of its issues are open. Close some, or raise it.
- `has waited for a human for`: Nothing in the fleet moves that issue. `fix` answers it: [`afkconvoy help humans`](help:humans).

- ``have reached the team's `max_open` ``: Open proposals on the team's repo fill its limit, so further proposals wait at `full`. `doctor` lists every PR under `proposals.open`, with the commands to merge or close it; the panel shows them under "With a human". Accept or close one to make room ([`afkconvoy help humans`](help:humans)).
- `is held off by a PR not the fleet's`: No worker starts: it would open a second PR. `fix` closes it, or merge it yourself.
- `is claimed but GitHub has it no more`: Deleted or transferred: its fleet's next tick releases it. `fix` is for one stopped.
- `the gate is slow`: On one host, the last 5 landings with a recorded gate run all took more than 80% of the gate limit. A tick opens one issue for the fleet to make the gate faster: `fix` shows it. Raising `gate_seconds` is no fix, nor is deleting or skipping tests.
- `the host runner did not move onto`: A newer release is installed where the host runner was started from, and it did not start, does not say its version, or the wait for ticks and a running exclusive command to end exceeded ten minutes: `evidence` says why, including which ticks or command held it. The host runner works on, on its own release, and tries that file again once it changes: install it again (`brew reinstall afkconvoy`), and `fix` shows whether it now says its version.

#### What `doctor` finds — info: nothing is held up

- `which nothing reads any more`: The repo config names `concurrency`, and a checkout's concurrency is said on its host instead (`afkconvoy run --help`): this checkout's fleet instance holds its own, or 3 where it says none, whatever the config names. Nothing is held up, even where the values differ. Where the checkout says none and the config names a different number, `fix` is the `run` that keeps the config's number on this host, then deleting the key; otherwise it is the deletion alone. Run that line on each host that needs to keep the config's number before the deletion reaches it, or that host holds 3.
- `moved since the stage`: A role or the team was pushed after a stage started: that worker goes by the older one, the next stage by the head. `afkconvoy doctor --help` says what moved is.
- `declares no gate limit`: The config sets no `gate_seconds`: the gate may run 3600 seconds before anything ends it. Set it to the most the gate should take: `fix` names the file and key.
- `is kept with no claim`: A worktree holds what the remote lacks, or an earlier release kept it. `fix` removes it, pushing first what only it holds: read `what` before you run it.

#### What a start refuses with — `plan`, `tick` and `run` check first, and start nothing

- `this host cannot work a fleet yet`: What `doctor` finds on a host, said at once: run each line after a colon.
- `cannot read the config file`: The repo has no config on the branch checked out. `afkconvoy config --help`.
- `the remote has no branch`: The config's `base_branch` is not on the remote. Push it: the fleet creates none.
- `is public: anyone can comment on its issues`: The checkout's tracker — its own repo, where it says none — is public. Say a private one with the line the refusal ends in, or make it private.
- `that push would be refused`: The base branch's protection requires a PR, checks or a named pusher, and a landing turn ends by pushing. Lift the rule, or pick another base branch.
- `the remote rejects the fleet's refs under both`: The remote takes neither hidden refs nor `convoy-*` branches, so no claim can be kept. A push rule of the remote's is what refuses: lift it for one of the two.
- A missing worker launch command is discovered automatically for a known harness in the worker's login shell and merged into the latest host kit. If resolution fails, install the named program or fix that shell's PATH. If login or required flags fail, follow the named harness's login command or update its explicit command in the host kit. An explicit command is never replaced by a default; running fleets read kit edits at their next worker launch.
- `cannot read the host kit`: Run `afkconvoy kit` on this host, or `run`, which writes it where there is none.
- `--worker-command is gone`: Run `afkconvoy kit` to edit this host's worker launch commands.
- `is no harness`: Use claude-code, pi, codex, dsh or kimi.

#### What neither says

- **An issue is not worked**: `afkconvoy plan` has it under `excluded`, with why. Remove what the reason names.
- **A changed role or team did not reach a worker**: It is not pushed to its default branch, or the stage had already started.
- **The labels were moved back, and the issue escalated again**: A label is not where an issue is: [`afkconvoy help humans`](help:humans).
- **A stage's verdict counted for nothing**: Its record names another stage than its claim was for. `afkconvoy show --issue <n>` says how each record was read; `afkconvoy send` puts the issue where it belongs.
- **Another host's fleet died**: Its claims go stale by themselves and are taken. Or: `afkconvoy takeover --help`.
- **Everything must stop now**: SIGTERM the host runner (`host_runner.pid` in any `run`'s answer), then close the workers' terminals in orca. Every issue keeps its labels and stage records: a later `run` goes on from where each one was.

### `afkconvoy help glossary`

Every term afkconvoy's help uses, each with its one definition and the words to avoid in its place. afkconvoy works a repo's ready GitHub-issue backlog unattended, from the command line: it dispatches one worktree-isolated coding agent per issue and lands their finished PRs on the base branch behind a local gate. It is a trimmed Rust port of the `afk-fleet` skill (`docs/adr/0001`).

#### Language

##### The fleet

**Fleet instance**:
One repo's fleet in its host's host runner, and everything it owns: the workers it started and the claims it holds, under an id minted when it starts. One host runs at most one per repo.
_Avoid_: launcher, coordinator, node, process (the host runner is the process)

**Host runner**:
A host's one long-running process of the fleet, holding a fleet instance for each checkout on its host's checkout list. `run` starts it in the background where none runs, and adds its checkout to it either way. `stop` takes one checkout off its list, and `stop --all`, or SIGTERM, stops it and keeps the list. Once a newer release is installed where it was started from, it moves onto it by itself between ticks once no exclusive command runs, on the same list, with its workers and work carried over (docs/adr/0032).
_Avoid_: daemon (a process outside the fleet), server (an MCP server, a model provider's), supervisor

**Checkout list**:
The checkouts a host's runner works, kept on that host and never pushed. The host runner converges on it: a checkout added is started, and a host runner started again starts every checkout on it. Each checkout on it may say its own **concurrency** and its **tracker** there, which a `run` that names them changes, and its fleet instance reads at each tick — a `run` that starts the host runner says the tracker there before it starts it, so that the host runner's start of the checkout from the list goes by it.
_Avoid_: registry, workspace list, projects (Codex's config key)

**Concurrency**:
How many claims a fleet instance holds at work at once on its host. It is its checkout's, said on the checkout list of the host that runs it, and 3 until that host says otherwise: what a host can carry — its cores, its memory, its logins — is no fact of the repo, so a repo config names none (`docs/adr/0025`).
_Avoid_: parallelism, workers (the processes it bounds), the repo's concurrency

**Tracker**:
The repo a fleet reads and writes its issues in: its checkout's own, until the checkout says another on the checkout list of its host (`run --tracker`), never pushed. Everything about an issue is the tracker's — its labels, its comments, its blockers, its escalation, its closing, and every issue the fleet opens — and every PR, branch, worktree, gate run and landing are the repo's. `#<n>` alone is the repo's own issue: the repo names a tracker's `<owner>/<tracker>#<n>` (`docs/adr/0027`). A public one is refused — the checkout's own repo too, where it says none — by every start's startup probe and by `run --tracker`, and a fleet instance whose tracker is made public is broken at its next check, within the hour one that found it private stands: anyone can comment on a public repo's issues, and so write what the fleet reads as its state and what its workers read as their task.
_Avoid_: issue repo, backlog (all the issues a repo has open), project (a GitHub Project)

**First start**:
The start of a checkout not yet on its host's checkout list, whose tracker and concurrency are settled with the user; on a host with no host settings yet, its host sleep is settled too. The agent explains the choices, sets up what needs no decision, and asks the user together for what does.
_Avoid_: onboarding, setup wizard

**Repo label**:
`repo:<owner>/<repo>`: what makes an issue of a tracker one of that repo's. A fleet whose tracker is another repo works only the issues there that carry its repo's, and gives it to every issue it opens, takes in or locks there; one carrying two is no fleet's. In a repo that is its own tracker, an issue carrying one is the repo's it names.
_Avoid_: component label, project label

**Broken**:
A fleet instance whose loop panicked or ended in an error — its tracker found public, say — or a start of which ended before its first tick while its checkout is on the checkout list, whoever started it: the host runner, from the list or again, or a `run`, which is told why — its startup probe no longer passing, say. It harms no other and stays on the checkout list, which only `stop` takes a checkout off: the host runner starts it again after a backoff — a minute, twice as long at each break in a row, half an hour at the most — or at once when a `run` of its checkout asks. It is **back** once such a start ended its first tick. A tick that fails is no break: the loop goes on.
_Avoid_: crashed, dead (a heartbeat past the lease), down (a harness that refuses every prompt)

**Host settings**:
What a host says for every fleet instance on it — whether it may be put to sleep and its sleep hours, the limits past which a worker is hot, the shares admission holds back at, the bound on an exclusive command holding others up, the number of worker lanes, the panel's port, the operator's directory a watch starts in and how often the host runner looks, the command that supplies a TypeSafe key for Jev's worker-health judgments — kept beside the checkout list and changed by any `run` that names one, for every fleet instance on the host at once.
_Avoid_: global config, runner flags

**Tick**:
One reconciliation pass: rebuild the working set from fleet state, then perform every transition it calls for, without waiting for the workers it started.
_Avoid_: cycle, poll, batch

**Plan**:
A tick stopped after its rebuild, which reports what an acting tick would do and leaves nothing written: its startup probe, when it makes one, is the only thing it pushes, and it deletes that.
_Avoid_: dry run, preview

**Startup probe**:
What `run`, `tick` and `plan` ask of a host and a repo before anything else: that every command the fleet needs is installed and logged in, that orca is running and knows the checkout, that the base branch exists and no rule of its protection refuses a push, that its tracker is not public, where the remote takes the fleet's refs, and whether it takes recorded gate runs. A host or a repo the fleet cannot work is refused here, not at its first tick or landing. `run` makes one at every start; one that passed stands for an hour on the host that made it, while the tracker the checkout says is the one it found private, and `tick` and `plan` make none while it does. A running fleet instance asks again whether its tracker is public as that hour ends, or as it says another.
_Avoid_: bootstrap, preflight, health check

**Ref layout**:
One of the two ways every ref the fleet writes is named: hidden refs (`refs/convoy/*`), or — only where the remote rejects those — ordinary branches (`convoy-*`), on which push-triggered CI fires.
_Avoid_: namespace, fallback mode

**Fleet state**:
The authoritative record of what is claimed, in flight, landed, parked and escalated. It lives entirely in GitHub — the issues in the fleet's tracker, the PRs, branches and refs in the repo — and no process holds it. A PR whose head is in another repository is no part of it: only a login with write access can push a branch to the repo, so a PR from one of its branches is a collaborator's, and one from a fork is anyone's. The fleet acts as if a fork's PR did not exist — none is landed, taken up, synced, closed, commented on or reported, none holds an issue off, and none on a team's repo is taken for a proposal.
_Avoid_: run state, memory (what a host holds resident, as under Hot worker)

**Working set**:
A tick's view of the fleet at one moment, derived from fleet state and dropped when the tick ends.
_Avoid_: session state

**Rebuild**:
The read-only pass at the top of every tick that derives the working set. Any fleet instance rebuilds the same working set from the same GitHub. It lists the remote once and asks GitHub a fixed number of times, however many issues are open, and however many repos' issues its tracker holds.
_Avoid_: refresh (a heartbeat is refreshed), resync

**Frontier**:
The issues of the fleet's tracker a worker can be started on now — of a tracker that is another repo, those carrying the repo's repo label and no other: open, carrying a flow label, not an epic, unclaimed, with no open blocker, and at a stage a role performs or whose `escalate` a consult is to rule on — or landing, with an open PR to land. In an unbound repo: carrying the ready label, with no open linked PR but one of the fleet's own that a released claim kept, not landed — which its worker takes up. While a fleet lock stands: of these, the lock issues only.
_Avoid_: queue (the exclusive queue of a host's heavy commands), backlog (all the issues a repo has open)

**Idle**:
A fleet instance with nothing to do now: it holds no claim — on an issue, a patrol's run, the proposal of a precedent or a cut — its frontier is empty. An escalated issue waiting for a human leaves it idle, and so does a patrol not yet due.
_Avoid_: drained, done (what a step or a command did), finished (a PR its worker is through with)

**Host sleep**:
A fleet instance putting its host to sleep: the host's local time is within its sleep hours, every fleet instance on the host has been idle for ten minutes, as its host runner holds how each stands, each has ticked once more and found nothing, no one has used the host's keyboard or mouse for ten minutes, the one that puts it to sleep has worked since the host last woke, and the host settings do not keep it awake. A host woken stays awake until some instance on it has worked again. The fleet never wakes a host: one put to sleep within its sleep hours sleeps on past their end.
_Avoid_: sleep (the wait between ticks), hibernate, suspend, shutdown

**Sleep hours**:
The hours of a host's local time its fleets may put it to sleep in: from 00:00 to 06:00 unless its host settings say others (`--host-sleep-hours 22:00-06:00`), the start included and the end not, past midnight where the end comes first, and any hour with `00:00-24:00`. A check for host sleep outside them keeps the host awake, says so, and is followed by the next as they start.
_Avoid_: quiet hours, night mode

**Base branch**:
The one branch a repo's fleet work is cut from and lands on.
_Avoid_: trunk, main, default branch (a team's or a role's repo is read at its own)

##### Teams and roles

**Role**:
A directory that defines one kind of worker: the rules it always works under, the limits it cannot cross, and the skills it can be asked to perform. It is a whole repo or a subdirectory of one. A worker starts in it, and is given nothing else of its repo.
_Avoid_: agent (as under Worker), persona, profile (as under DSH profile)

**Team**:
A directory that names a set of roles and holds the workflows, patrols and precedents they work by. It is a whole repo or a subdirectory of one, and its roles may be directories of the same repo.
_Avoid_: org, crew, squad

**Team rules**:
The rules every role of a team works under, whatever its own rules add. They say how the team works, and hold in any repo bound to it; what one codebase asks is that repo's to say, and what one kind of worker does is its role's.
_Avoid_: global rules, shared rules

**Admission**:
Whether a tick starts new workers on its host: not while the host is past a share of its load, below its share of memory free, or low on free disk under the checkout. What it holds back stays on the frontier for the next tick; workers already running and the worker a declared verdict starts are never held back. The shares have defaults taken from the host's cores, memory and disk, and the host can say its own in its host settings. Holding back for one reason — the load, memory or disk — at every tick past a span (ten minutes, or the host's own) calls for the host's watch, once an **episode**: the episode ends once admission has admitted for five minutes. Holding back for reasons that change starts none. Memory pressure is observed independently: held past the same span, it calls for the host's watch for memory, once an episode ending after five minutes without pressure; it changes no admission decision.
_Avoid_: throttling, backpressure

**Host user's skills and rules**:
The skills and the rules the host's own user has for a harness, which a session they start by hand loads: a worker of a bound repo is given them beside its role's, unless its team file says `host_user: false`. A role may say it for itself, whatever the team says: `reviewer: { dir: ./roles/reviewer, host_user: false }` in `roles`; a role named by its directory alone takes the team's. Its role's skills win over them, and the brief, its role's rules, the team rules and the repo's own rules win over theirs. DSH alone may load those too when its role chooses the host user's DSH profile.
_Avoid_: global rules, user config, personal skills

**DSH profile**:
What a DSH worker loads of bundles, plugins, MCP servers, patches, themes and settings: the fleet's own (`dsh_profile: fleet`, the default), or the host user's `dsh-tui` profile (`dsh_profile: host-user`). The team chooses for every role; a role may choose its own, independently of `host_user`, and both keep the guard and the role's limits.
_Avoid_: provider profile, persona

**Bound repo**:
A repo whose config names a team. An unbound repo has no roles and one fixed path for every issue: one worker, then a turn that lands its PR.
_Avoid_: team mode, managed repo

**Guard**:
The check made before each thing a worker does, refusing what its role or its stage may not do — and, of a watch, what crosses the bounds of any unattended worker. It stops a worker that errs, not one that means to get past it.
_Avoid_: permission (what a harness's own settings deny), sandbox (what a harness may shut a worker's commands in)

##### Workflows

**Workflow**:
The stages one issue passes through and where each verdict leads, ending in a landed PR or in nothing more to do.
_Avoid_: pipeline, process (a program that is running)

**Flow label**:
The label that names the workflow an issue follows: `flow:<name>`, unless the workflow's file names another with `label` — the ready label, say, so that an issue opened the usual way is worked. A bound repo's issue is the fleet's to work only while it carries one; there the ready label is one only where a workflow names it.
_Avoid_: type label

**Intake**:
Putting a flow label on an issue. A human does it on GitHub; a worker does it through the fleet, which records who did and holds the number of such issues still open under a limit — of a tracker that is another repo, the repo's issues alone, each of which intake gives the repo label.
_Avoid_: enroll, admit (a tick starting new workers on a host not busy: admission), triage

**Stage**:
One step of a workflow: one skill of one role, performed by one new worker — or a decision waited for from a human.
_Avoid_: step (one thing a tick does), phase, state (fleet state and worker state are terms)

**Stage record**:
The comment a stage leaves on its issue: what it produced, its verdict, the versions of the role and team it ran under, and the harness its worker ran on, with the model where it was started on one. A human who declares for a stage, rules on it or sends the issue to it leaves one too, which says a human did; so does the fleet, for a stage that runs again because a fleet lock closed. The stage an issue is at is derived from these and stored nowhere.
_Avoid_: handoff note, log (the tick log; what a gate prints), stage label

**Position**:
Where an issue is in its workflow: at a stage a worker is to perform, waiting on a human, with a consult, parked, landing, ended, or escalating. It is derived from the stage records each tick and stored nowhere.
_Avoid_: state (as under Stage), status (the status board; a key of what a command answers), current stage

**Rework**:
A stage running again because a later stage rejected its work or a consult ruled on it. It is counted per issue from the stage records, from where a human last ruled on the issue or sent it to a stage.
_Avoid_: retry, round, attempt (what an issue was worked into before a fresh start)

**Breaker**:
A limit on rework — in total for an issue, or as rejections in a row by one stage — past which the issue escalates.
_Avoid_: retry limit, circuit

**Consult**:
A worker in a senior role explicitly named by a team's stage, asked before escalation about the work. It rules, sends, closes, parks or lets the issue through, and never commits, pushes or changes the host; the same hand-off again, its own failure, a fleet fault and any hand-off with no named consult escalate for the host's watch to answer.
_Avoid_: review (a stage may be named it), second opinion, handoff, default consult

**Fleet fault**:
A hand-off caused by the fleet, its harness or its host: a worker start that failed again, a worktree trust gap. It escalates at once, in a bound repo and an unbound one alike, because the fix is on the host; a worker gone silent had its brief, so its hand-off is about the work.
_Avoid_: infrastructure failure, system fault

**Ruling**:
What a consult or a human decides on an issue handed on. The stage runs again under it; a human's also hands the issue back to the fleet and starts the rework counts over, a consult's starts none over.
_Avoid_: answer (what a command prints), decision (what a `by: human` stage waits for), override

**Precedent**:
A ruling kept so that later stages follow it instead of escalating. A worker proposes it; a human accepts it.
_Avoid_: rule (a role's rules and the team rules; the command `rule`), policy, guideline

**Proposal**:
One human's ruling put forward as a precedent: a PR on the team's repo that appends one entry to its precedents file. A ruling gets one; a human merging it is what accepts the precedent.
_Avoid_: suggestion, draft (a roster `afkconvoy draft` writes), candidate (a key of what `recovery` answers)

**Split**:
Parking an issue on issues its own stage opened. When they have all closed, that stage runs again and judges the whole.
_Avoid_: decompose, epic (an issue under an epic label), fan out

**Patrol**:
A role run on a schedule rather than for an issue. It opens issues and takes them in; it writes no code. It is due once its interval has passed since its last run, and — where its file says `max_runs_a_day` — while fewer than that many of its runs started in the last 24 hours, rolling. Where it says `max_landed_a_day`, it is also held while that many issues it opened were closed as completed in the last rolling 24 hours, until enough completions are 24 hours old to fall below the bound. Its run takes one slot until its worker declares it over, which the next tick acts on; a worker that never does is ended once it is gone or has stopped for a grace period. Each run has a checkout of its own, removed as the run ends unless it failed.
_Avoid_: cron, job, scheduled worker

**Fleet lock**:
An open issue carrying the lock label, in a bound repo or an unbound one — of a tracker that is another repo, and the repo label of the repo whose fleet it holds: no other repo's fleet that works the same tracker. While one stands the fleet works lock issues only — nothing else is dispatched, no PR of another issue lands, and workers already running are left alone, what they declare being acted on afterwards — and closing the last one ends it. A stage's `escalate` or failure the lock explains — declared before it closed, and not acted on since — is then not carried out: the stage runs again, which is no rework.
_Avoid_: freeze, pause (a harness paused on a host, as under Host kit), kill switch

##### Workers

**Harness**:
The program a worker is a session of: it runs a model, with tools, on the work it is handed. Claude Code, pi, Codex, DeepSeek Harness (DSH) and Kimi Code are harnesses. The host kit's order chooses the first eligible one; a role's limits and range constrain eligibility.
_Avoid_: agent (as under Worker), coding agent (as under Worker), CLI, provider (whose models a harness runs)

**Roster**:
A team's list, for each of its roles, of the harnesses and models that role's workers may run, with what each model is good at and how an issue is to be cast among them. It is committed with the team, written under the team file's `roster`: for each role it names, a `run` listing `{ harness, model, good_at }` as eligibility constraints — a harness named with no model allows any model the host kit holds for it — and a `cast` saying how to cast among them. A role's **range** on a host is its entry cut to the host kit, in the host kit's order, less each harness the role holds no limits for while it holds limits for another; a role it names no entry for ranges over the host kit, less the same — and so does one whose entry matches nothing in the host kit, which `check`, `plan` and `doctor` name — and an unbound repo, having no team, over the host kit whole. A role whose range is empty, holding limits for no harness the host kit holds, refuses no start: no worker of it is started, its stages wait while it lasts, and every other stage goes on. A stage, a patrol and a config name no harness and no model: what a worker runs is its role's range's to say. A roster is drafted by `afkconvoy draft` from a host kit into the team's working tree — every role, every harness and model in the host kit's order, what the host kit's first model says each is good at and how to cast — and committed by a human; the fleet never changes it. An entry that names a model the host kit holds by no name is named with the nearest names and given one issue in the team’s repo for its own fleet to correct.
_Avoid_: harness config, model table, routing rules

**Host kit**:
The harnesses this host can start and their models, each in order of preference, with each harness's worker launch command and what research says of each model. Writing it lists each harness's models and sends none a prompt. Each model is held by the id its harness lists, with the names its listing shows it by and those research ties to it with a dated source. A harness found and listed is held at once and starts workers on its **default model** until research places its models: a model is placed once research ranks it with a dated source. The watch researches models awaiting research and records sourced placements or settlements; research runs alongside its other work or starts the watch alone at most once a day. A model that fails at work is found by worker health, not by the kit. These orders are this machine's sole priority for every checkout; the kit also holds whether automatic model casting is enabled, off until the user enables it.

Research states: `research pending` is a newly listed model awaiting dated research; `not researched` is an older release's model with no dated answer, also awaiting research. Neither is started on. A settled model has a dated source and a reason research found it unsuited to workers: it is not placed, is named by no unplaced-model finding and starts no watch. The finding names exactly the models awaiting research, including models held with no dated answer; every one can be placed or settled through `afkconvoy kit --research <file>`. Placements and settlements survive routine relisting; an identity dropped from the kit and later listed anew awaits research again.
_Avoid_: roster (the team's), host config, inventory

**Default model**:
What a harness's own login runs when a worker is started with no model flag, which the fleet cannot name. A harness the host kit holds with no model placed — none listed yet, or research pending — starts its workers on it, Codex too.
_Avoid_: fallback model, `default` alone (a model id Claude Code lists)

**Codex effort**:
The reasoning effort a Codex worker takes from the host user's own Codex settings at its start, or Codex's model default where the user says none. It is independent of the fleet's model selection and is no setting of the fleet.
_Avoid_: fleet effort, role effort

**Casting**:
An issue's model labels, put on by its caster or a human, selecting a matching model only within the harness chosen by kit order and role eligibility; legacy harness labels never choose a harness. Labels survive switches and faults, and a model label applies again whenever its harness is selected and holds it.
_Avoid_: assignment (a GitHub assignee), routing, dispatch (starting a worker)

**Caster**:
A worker in no role that chooses models for ready issues, only on a host whose kit enables automatic casting and only where a stage's selected harness has several models and no matching model label. It adds model labels while preserving earlier labels and human casting; an issue waits at most ten minutes before dispatch on its range's first model.
_Avoid_: assigner, router, dispatcher

**Worker**:
A session of one harness, started in one role to perform one stage of one issue — or, after its last stage, to land its PR in a turn — in that issue's worktree, and to report through GitHub. In an unbound repo it has no role and owns its issue from start to landing. It is ended — its terminal closed — by the step that ends what it was started for: its stage, its claim, or its run.
_Avoid_: agent (whoever reads the help; and a worker, to whoever has not met the term), subagent, child (an issue a split opened)

**Switch**:
Moving a harness, or one of its models and that model's harness, to the first position in this machine's host kit while retaining the other entries' relative order and contents. A known installed harness it does not hold is added on its stock worker launch command with no model, on its default model, and listed and researched only after the switch answers; no model is sent a prompt. Every checkout follows these orders; existing workers continue only when explicitly targeted, preserving their scene and claims and starting no replacement until the old writer is confirmed ended.
_Avoid_: harness change (what a new casting makes)

**Worker launch command**:
The shell string every worker of one harness is started with, in a fleet instance: one for each harness its workers run. The host kit says it, per harness, kept on the host at `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/afkconvoy/kit.json` or `$HOME/.config/afkconvoy/kit.json` and written by `afkconvoy kit`; each launch reads its latest command, or discovers and records a known harness's stock command when none is held; a start checks that of every harness it could be asked for, and starts no worker when one cannot be started. In an unbound repo it is opaque but for what the fleet adds: its harness's model flag where the worker runs a model — its issue's casting or the host kit's first — and its harness's worktree-trust setup, so every worker starts trusting its worktree and none waits on a folder-trust prompt. Every worker starts under `nice`, with a `TMPDIR` of its worktree's own: a link, `/tmp/afkconvoy-<uid>/<16 hex digits>`, to `.afkconvoy-tmp` in the worktree, short enough for a socket's path however long the worktree's is, and gone with the worktree once nothing started with it runs. A Codex worker's model is always the fleet's selection; its effort is the host user's Codex effort. A session's saved choice belongs to that session alone and chooses nothing for a later worker. In a bound repo the fleet adds to it what puts the worker in its role.
_Avoid_: agent command, provider profile

**Worker state**:
Whether a worker is busy or has stopped, as its harness reports it to the worker backend — or, where the backend has no report of it, as its terminal's last output shows. Stopped never means finished.
_Avoid_: liveness, status (as under Position)

**Task refusal**:
A harness's fixed refusal message on a worker's screen: it refuses this issue, by rule, and the worker continues on the next harness of the host kit that can start for its role. The issue remembers the harness at every later stage and start; other issues may still run it. With no harness left for the issue, it escalates at once with the refusal's words as evidence.
_Avoid_: account fault, model fault, failed task

**Capacity stop**:
A worker stopped by its harness's fixed message that its selected model is at capacity. It is transient and belongs to that worker: the harness remains available to other workers.
_Avoid_: quota fault (an account's usage limit), task refusal (a harness refusing this issue)

**Verdict**:
What ends a stage, declared on the issue by whoever performed it: `pass`, `reject`, `blocked`, `already-satisfied`, or `escalate`. Opening a PR declares nothing.
_Avoid_: outcome (what a worker leaves on GitHub: its landed PR, or its verdict), result, needs-human

**Silent worker**:
A worker that stopped, declared nothing, and for the grace period showed no sign of life — its terminal's output, a commit, a file touched, being started or nudged — while waiting on no background work of its own: a shell or a monitor it started that its harness shows still running, or a command of its in the exclusive queue. One waiting on such work is not silent until that work ends and it stays still past its nudge, or until it has waited longer than the gate limit.
_Avoid_: hung, idle (a fleet instance with nothing to do)

**Hot worker**:
A worker whose processes — every one started with its `TMPDIR`, and every one under those, but a server shared by the host that it started: one handed to pid 1 that works outside its worktree — take more than their share of the host, or whose worktree has outgrown its build. Its processes: more than half the host's cores (one at the least) held for two minutes, more than a quarter of its memory resident, or more written to disk in ten minutes than a tenth of the disk free (a GiB at the least). Its worktree: what git ignores there past `OUTGROWN_TIMES` its **fresh build** and past `OUTGROWN_FLOOR` — judged once its first green `afkconvoy gate` has recorded that fresh build. The host can say other limits in its host settings (`--hot-cores`, `--hot-memory`, `--hot-written`). `run` samples each worker every ten seconds, with no root, and measures its worktree every minute; one that has stayed under every limit for five minutes — its worktree back under the rule among them — stops being hot, and that ends its **episode**: hot again later is a new one. Memory pressure makes no worker hot: held past the host resource span, it calls for the host's watch.
_Avoid_: hog

**Watch**:
The operator on its host, started by its host runner when a **look** at the host holds something an operator would act on, in the operator's own directory where the host names one, otherwise as the **stock watch** in afkconvoy's own directory. The stock watch stands in where no operator directory is named: its one short instruction is to find what holds the fleets' work back, fix it with the watch's authority, check that the work goes on and say what it did. An operator's directory supplies its own rules, with none of the stock instruction added. A look is `afkconvoy doctor --all --since <until of the last look>`, every five minutes or as the host settings say (`--watch-every`): the fleet's own code, which runs no model. What starts a watch: a hot worker, admission held back for one reason past its span, memory pressure past that span, an issue waiting on a human, a finding that holds something up (no `info`), a fleet instance not alive or broken, a failed tick or a step failed since, a worker whose health observation is past its time. Each starts at most one watch in its **episode**, which lasts while each look still holds it. A watch is one agent session, given its brief as a file — the look, why it started and what earlier watches on the same items did — on the harness this host last started a worker on that took its brief, then the host kit's order, never one paused or with a fault on record; started trusted and in its harness's non-interactive mode, so that nothing it runs waits on a prompt. What it printed is kept as what it did. A watch whose harness gives out — its own words for a usage limit, or an exit that failed — is ended and continued on the next harness that can start it, with the same look and what it did so far, one session at a time; the fault is recorded, and the harness is skipped until its probe answers. One watch runs on a host at a time: no look is taken while it runs, and a host runner started again keeps the one it finds running. An hour bounds it, its continuations together, and it has the authority and the bounds of a watch. Its start, its end and each thing it did are lines of every tick log of the host; `doctor` says the one running and what the last one did, and a finding where none could start (`docs/adr/0030`).
Its authority spans every repo on the host's checkout list: it fixes the host and hands an issue escalated for a fleet fault back once its cause is gone; makes a lasting fix in a checkout of its own of any listed repo, through that repo's landing turn; and, where the fix must reach an installed tool, has that repo cut a version after landing, lets the host runner move onto it and checks the fault on the new version. It answers escalations with the same commands as a human, whose effect and rework counts its answer has. Every watch leaves spending money or needing an account, a credential or a person's hands; what cannot be undone; taking a secret or private data off the host; and changing what a product is for or who it is for with a human, and records each without acting on it.
_Avoid_: patrol (a role run on a schedule that writes no code), supervisor (the host runner is the process)

**Exclusive queue**:
The host runner's FIFO queue for heavy commands across its fleets. Commands run in worker lanes, as many as the host settings allow. A turn holds its lane through landing; one repo holds at most one turn at once. A light gate takes a turn in its repo's own lane.
_Avoid_: gate queue

**Nudge**:
The one line the fleet types at a stopped worker with no outcome, telling it to carry on. Sent once for silence; a capacity stop may call for another after a longer wait.
_Avoid_: ping, reminder, retry

**Restart**:
Replacing a silent worker with a new one in the same worktree and the same role, with its PR, branch and worktree untouched. Made once, and only for a worker waiting to land its PR.
_Avoid_: retry, re-dispatch

**Continuation**:
Recovering a claim whose worker died from the progress that survived: its worktree if still on this host, else its pushed branch, else a fresh start from the base branch.
_Avoid_: resume, checkpoint restore

**Wake**:
A signal that ends the sleep between ticks of its host's fleet instance early: every command that changes fleet state sends one as it ends — a worker's last among them, once its outcome is on GitHub — naming itself and what it acted on, and carrying no state. `gh` sends none: whoever hands the fleet work sends one with `afkconvoy wake` after the issues they opened with it. The `run` that hears it answers at once, naming the tick it starts or the tick in progress it follows.
_Avoid_: notification, callback, done signal

##### Claims

**Claim**:
The atomic lock marking one issue as owned by one fleet instance. Its creation succeeds for exactly one instance. It takes one slot of the concurrency while its worker is at work, and none once a verdict is declared under it: it is still held until that verdict is acted on, and a worker started under it again takes a slot as any start does.
_Avoid_: assignee, assignment, lock (the fleet lock)

**Heartbeat**:
The timestamp a fleet instance publishes for itself while it holds claims, stamped with its host. A claim is live while its owner's heartbeat is within the lease. A `run` told to stop while it holds no claim removes its own; a start removes the dead ones that hold nothing: those of the instances it took from, its own host's past the lease, and anyone's older than a day.
_Avoid_: ping, keepalive

**Orphaned claim**:
A claim of this fleet instance with no PR and no live worker. It is recovered by continuation, never released.
_Avoid_: stuck issue, zombie

**Stale claim**:
Another fleet instance's claim whose heartbeat is past the lease. It is the only claim a fleet takes from another host unattended.
_Avoid_: dead claim, abandoned claim

**Takeover**:
Taking another fleet instance's claims — on issues, on patrols' runs, on proposals — without waiting for the lease. It happens unconditionally at start for claims stamped with this host, and by explicit command for another host's. A claim taken — by a takeover, or as a stale claim — is still the claim it was created as: what was declared under it stands.
_Avoid_: failover, stale reclaim

##### Outcomes

**Park**:
Recording a dependency a worker discovered as a blocker on its issue and releasing the claim, so the frontier holds the issue back until the blocker closes.
_Avoid_: defer, snooze, hold (a fleet instance holds its claims)

**Escalate**:
Handing an issue on with its reason and answer line, its flow or ready label swapped for the escalate label, and its claim released. The host's watch answers it with the operator's authority, through the same commands as a human; only money, an account, a credential or a person's hands; what cannot be undone; a secret or private data leaving the host; and a change of what a product is for or who it is for stay with a human.
_Avoid_: fail (what a command, a gate or one thing a tick does may), retry

**Status board**:
The single comment on a claimed issue that shows a human how far along it is, and what the afkconvoy that works it was built from. It is rendered from fleet state and never read back.
_Avoid_: progress log, worklog

**Panel**:
The one web page that shows a human where every fleet of a host stands: the host itself, what waits for a human across its repos, and for each repo its workflows as the lines of their stages, the issues at work, queued and held back at each, and their landing turns. The host runner serves it, made anew from what each tick read; it is never read back.
_Avoid_: dashboard, status page, status board (the comment on one issue), UI

**Tick log**:
The file a fleet instance keeps on its own host: one line as it starts, a line as each tick starts — with why: its timer, a wake and the command that sent it, the fleet instance's start, or a follow-up — and one as it ends — what it did, and what changed on GitHub or by another host since the tick before where it acted on that — plus the lines of the events that reached the fleet instance: a wake heard during a tick, a check for host sleep, the host waking, being told to stop. Every command that changes fleet state, whoever runs it, appends a line of its own to the file of its host and repo as it acts — the command, the issue, who ran it, and how it came out or that it failed — whether a fleet instance is there or not. Each line is appended whole, and only the fleet instance cuts the file back: it keeps every line of the last day, and never fewer than 200 lines nor more than 5000. It is a log and not fleet state: nothing reads it to decide what the fleet does.
_Avoid_: state file, journal, history

**Finding**:
One thing `doctor` says is wrong with the fleet on this host, with how bad it is, what shows it, its fix — a line to run, or a file and the key in it to edit — and the help topic that explains it. `doctor` fixes none itself.
_Avoid_: diagnosis (a worker health assessment), alert, warning (one of its severities), error (what a command that failed answers with)

##### Landing

**Gate**:
The repo's build-and-test command. It is the only machine verification a change must pass before it lands.
_Avoid_: CI (what a push to an ordinary branch starts), checks (what `check` and the startup probe make), local CI

**Gate limit**:
How long the gate may run. A run that reaches it is ended and is red. A repo declares it; nothing learns it from past runs.
_Avoid_: timeout (what a run that reached it did), budget, baseline

**Recorded gate run**:
The evidence that the gate passed on one committed tree, with how long the run took and on which host, made by the tool that saw the exit code and kept where every host can read it.
_Avoid_: gate cache, CI status

**Slow gate**:
What the gate is when its recent runs for the base branch, on one host, all took most of the gate limit. The fleet opens one issue that says so, and no second while that one is open.
_Avoid_: regression, drift, creep

**Sync**:
Bringing a branch up to date by merging into it. Nothing is ever rebased.
_Avoid_: rebase, update branch

**Turn**:
One command's uninterrupted merge, gate, recording and landing of an open PR, starting on the base branch's current tip. Red, a conflict or a rejected push ends it with nothing landed.
_Avoid_: landing slot, merge queue

**Land**:
Pushing the merge commit a turn gated and recorded green onto the base branch as a fast-forward, and closing the issue it completes. Issue workers, a workflow's landing worker, watches and cuts all land in a turn.
_Avoid_: join, enqueue

**Repair**:
A change the fleet starts to restore a red base tip or finish retained work from an older release. Its operator worker owns an issue and a worktree, works outside product workflows and human stages, and lands through the same recorded turn as every other change.
_Avoid_: manual repair

**Cut**:
The run that makes a new version of a repo from its base branch: it sets the version, lands it, tags it, and publishes and installs it. An idle fleet starts one when landed work is past the newest version tag, or when the repo declares its initial version and the remote has no version tag; each cut belongs to one host, and a failed cut holds later cuts back until its failure is answered.
_Avoid_: release (a claim's last step, and `afkconvoy release`), publish (a heartbeat's), deploy
